lots.what_it_is: Mahogany crossbanded and line-inlaid serving table or sideboard with a low stage back, three frieze drawers with brass handles and carved fluted blocks between them, a pierced brass fret band along the frieze, reeded turned legs with brass collars on brass castors. 19th century or later in Regency style. No maker's mark seen. The brass fret band, reeded legs with brass collars and the long shallow box form are all typical of square piano cases, so it may be a converted square piano. That is my reading of the photos, not confirmed.

The only category signal is Denhams 10 Apr 2025, lot 964, a Georgian bleached and inlaid mahogany bow front sideboard that sold for GBP 50 (about AUD 94 at 1.889). That shows how cheap small period sideboards can go in the UK. It is not a comp and sets no maximum. All-in cost would be hammer x 1.22.

The researcher misread which lot the price sat under. Dropped, and lot 982 has no price so it is not usable as UNSOLD either. (2) Smith and Singer AU0759/131 (page opened with curl): Regency mahogany and satinwood serpentine sideboard, estimate AUD 4,000-6,000. A genuine, much larger and better piece, and an estimate only. Not the same item. (3) Smith and Singer KEITHOKEY/327 (page opened with curl): Australian cedar and casuarina sideboard c.1825, estimate AUD 20,000-30,000. A rare colonial piece, not comparable. (4) sellingantiques.co.uk 1127686: the page returns HTTP 404. It was snippet only before, so dropped. Searches: my WebSearch budget for this session is used up, so I could not look for new comps, for example converted square piano sideboards.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: the width across the top is about 1.8 times the height from the top of the back to the floor. If H is 100 cm, it is more like 170-180 cm wide than the catalogue's 108 cm. Photos 2 and 6: the top is crossbanded with stringing and has a low stage back. Photos 3 and 4: brass fret band on the frieze, carved fluted blocks between the drawers, brass collars on reeded legs, and brass castors, all consistent with a square piano case. Age wear to the top. One key in a drawer.
lots.condition: Looks sound from the photos. General wear and some fading on the top. The brass fret band looks complete where it can be seen. No view inside the drawers or of the back.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the width? The photos suggest well over 108 cm. Is this a converted square piano case (any name board, tuning pin holes or piano frame inside)? Can you send photos inside the drawers, showing the joints, and of the back?

lots.what_it_is: Oil on board, misty lake with a rocky bluff and two figures in a rowboat, 30 x 46 cm, in an ornate gilt gesso frame with a linen slip. The catalogue says it is signed Haughton Forrest. The enlarged photo 5 shows a dark cursive signature low left in the grass. It is consistent in shape and length with 'H Forrest', but I cannot read it with confidence. Size, format and handling match Forrest's standard 30 x 46 cm Tasmanian lake boards. Credible but not confirmed. It could turn out to be 'attributed'.

lots.guide_summary: 5 sold, 2 unsold, 0 asking, all AUD, no conversion. The sold range runs from 3,750 for an 'attributed' 30 x 46 board with a doubtful signature (Lawsons, Sep 2026), through 6,250 for a signed generic Lake Scene (Lawsons, Dec 2025), to 15,000-17,000 for named Tasmanian views with provenance. Two signed 30 x 46 boards passed at last bids of 5,250 and 6,000. Lawsons results match the last bid, so they look like hammer prices. The Davidson and Leonard Joel results are well above the last bid shown, so their basis is unclear.
lots.working: Keep: the lowest surviving close SOLD is AUD 3,750 (the attributed 30 x 46 board, Lawsons 28 Sep 2026). I use this deliberately because this signature is not confirmed. 3,750 / 1.22 = 3,073.8, rounded down to 3,070. All-in 3,070 x 1.22 = 3,745. If the signature is confirmed genuine at the viewing, the next floor is the signed Lake Scene at 6,250 / 1.22 = 5,122.9, which rounds down to 5,120. Treat that only as a ceiling once the signature and back have been checked. Flip: assume a conservative resale at the attributed level of 3,750 hammer at a Sydney house. Less 15% vendor commission (562.50) and about $150 for delivery, insurance and photography leaves 3,037.50. 3,037.50 / 2.44 = 1,244.9, rounded down to 1,240. All-in 1,240 x 1.22 = 1,513. Pickup only, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: The SOLD evidence is good (5 close sales, pages opened), but the signature cannot be read with confidence in the photos, and the rules put an unread mark at Low. Attribution is the main value driver: 3,750 attributed against 6,250 or more signed.

(3) Deutscher and Hackett 'Lake Scene' 2010 AUD 8,400: the URL opens a different D+H sale page, where lot 104 Haughton Forrest Lake Scene shows estimate 12,000-16,000 and no price. The attributed Lawsons Sep 2026 lot has now sold, so it is moved to SOLD. lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 5, cropped and contrast-boosted: a dark cursive signature low left in the grass, about 5 letters after an initial, consistent in length and form with 'H Forrest' but not legible. Photos 1 to 4: a misty lake with a sandstone-like bluff, a rowboat with two figures, and birds. The handling of foliage and mist fits Forrest's lake boards. Ornate gilt gesso frame with a linen slip, very like the frame on the Lawsons attributed example. No photo of the back.
lots.condition: The paint surface looks clean and even, with no tears or obvious retouching visible at this resolution. The frame has rubbing and small gesso losses to the ornament. The back has not been seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you send a sharp, raking-light close-up of the lower left signature and full photos of the back of the board (labels, inscriptions, stamps, Forrest Project catalogue number)? Is it definitely on board? Any known provenance or restoration? Is Armitage cataloguing it as by Haughton Forrest or attributed?

lots.what_it_is: Small sepia wash drawing, about 17 x 26 cm, of a Lake District style scene with a lake, mountains, cattle watering and figures. Cream mat, gilt slip, and a wide burr (birdseye) Huon pine veneered frame. Armitage catalogues it only as 'attributed John Glover'. The composition fits Glover's English manner, but many followers and pupils worked in this sepia style. The pencil inscription on the backing is not legible, so the attribution is unproven. The Huon pine frame has real value in itself.
